\[
\boxed{
(P_{m,k},N_{m,k})=
\begin{cases}
\left(2^{\,m-k/2-1},\,0\right),& k\ \text{even},\\[2mm]
\left(2^{\,m-(k+5)/2},\,2^{\,m-(k+5)/2}\right),& k\ \text{odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]

Let
\[
u=x+y,\qquad v=y.
\]
This is an invertible change of variables modulo \(2^m\), and
\[
x^2+2xy+(1+2^k)y^2=u^2+2^k v^2.
\]
Also
\[
rx+sy=ru+(s-r)v.
\]
Thus
\[
A_{m,k}(r,s)=G_m(r)\,H_{m,k}(s-r),
\]
where
\[
G_m(r)=\sum_{u\bmod 2^m} e^{2\pi i(u^2-ru)/2^m},
\]
and
\[
H_{m,k}(t)=\sum_{v\bmod 2^m} e^{2\pi i(2^k v^2-tv)/2^m}.
\]

Pairing \(u\) with \(u+2^{m-1}\) shows \(G_m(r)=0\) unless \(r\) is even. If \(r=2a\), then
\[
G_m(2a)=e^{-2\pi i a^2/2^m}g_m,
\qquad
g_m=\sum_{u\bmod 2^m}e^{2\pi i u^2/2^m}.
\]
For \(m\ge2\),
\[
g_m=2^{(m+1)/2}e^{\pi i/4}.
\]

Similarly, writing \(t=s-r\), splitting \(v=w+j2^{m-k}\) shows \(H_{m,k}(t)=0\) unless \(2^k\mid t\). If \(t=2^k q\), then
\[
H_{m,k}(t)=2^k G_{m-k}(q).
\]
Since \(m-k\ge3\), this is nonzero only when \(q=2b\), i.e.
\[
s-r\equiv 0\pmod{2^{k+1}}.
\]
For such \(r=2a\) and \(s-r=2^{k+1}b\),
\[
A_{m,k}(r,s)=C\exp\left(2\pi i\left(\frac14-\frac{a^2}{2^m}-\frac{b^2}{2^{m-k}}\right)\right),
\]
with \(C>0\).

Therefore \(A_{m,k}(r,s)\) is positive iff
\[
a^2+2^k b^2\equiv 2^{m-2}\pmod{2^m},
\]
and negative iff
\[
a^2+2^k b^2\equiv 3\cdot 2^{m-2}\pmod{2^m}.
\]
Here
\[
a\bmod 2^{m-1},\qquad b\bmod 2^{m-k-1}.
\]

It remains to count these congruences.

If \(k\) is odd, the two terms \(a^2\) and \(2^k b^2\) have opposite parity of 2-adic valuation, so no lower-order cancellation is possible. The relevant contributions modulo \(4\) after factoring \(2^{m-2}\) are \(0\) or \(1\) from one square and \(0\) or \(2\) from the other. Hence the residues \(1\) and \(3\) occur equally often, giving
\[
P_{m,k}=N_{m,k}
=2^{\lfloor (m-2)/2\rfloor+\lfloor (m-k-2)/2\rfloor}
=2^{m-(k+5)/2}.
\]

If \(k\) is even, write \(k=2e\). Then
\[
a^2+2^k b^2=a^2+(2^e b)^2.
\]
The congruence reduces to counting
\[
X^2+Y^2\equiv c\,2^{m-k-2}\pmod{2^{m-k}},
\qquad c\in\{1,3\}.
\]
A sum of two squares modulo a power of \(2\), when divided by its exact power of \(2\), is never \(3\bmod 4\). Thus \(N_{m,k}=0\). For \(c=1\), the count is
\[
2^{m-k-1}
\]
for \((X,Y)\), and there are \(2^e\) lifts for \(a\). Therefore
\[
P_{m,k}=2^e\cdot 2^{m-k-1}=2^{m-k/2-1}.
\]

So
\[
\boxed{
(P_{m,k},N_{m,k})=
\begin{cases}
\left(2^{\,m-k/2-1},\,0\right),& k\ \mathrm{even},\\[2mm]
\left(2^{\,m-(k+5)/2},\,2^{\,m-(k+5)/2}\right),& k\ \mathrm{odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]
